authors.name: Jiawei Chen
affiliation: College of Systems Engineering, National University of Defense Technology, Changsha, China

p: Jiawei Chen received the B.S. degree in civil engineering from The Ohio State University, Columbus, OH, USA, in 2019, and the joint M.S. degree in civil engineering and in computer science and engineering from Georgia Institute of Technology, Atlanta, GA, USA, in 2022. He is currently pursuing the Ph.D. degree in management science and engineering with the National University of Defense Technology, Changsha, China.
His research interests include scheduling, reinforcement learning, computational intelligence, large language models, and evolutionary algorithms.

p: Witold Pedrycz (Life Fellow, IEEE) is currently a Professor at the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, University of Alberta, Edmonton, AB, Canada. He is also with the Systems Research Institute of the Polish Academy of Sciences, Warsaw, Poland. His main research directions involve computational intelligence, granular computing, and machine learning.

Dr. Pedrycz is a Foreign Member of the Polish Academy of Sciences and a fellow of the Royal Society of Canada. He was a recipient of several awards, including the Norbert Wiener award from the IEEE Systems, Man, and Cybernetics Society, the IEEE Canada Computer Engineering Medal, the Cajastur Prize for Soft Computing from the European Centre for Soft Computing, the Killam Prize, the Fuzzy Pioneer Award from the IEEE Computational Intelligence Society, and the 2019 Meritorious Service Award from the IEEE Systems Man and Cybernetics Society. He serves as the Editor-in-Chief for WIREs Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery (Wiley).

authors.name: Feiran Wang
affiliation: College of Systems Engineering, National University of Defense Technology, Changsha, China

p: Feiran Wang received the master’s degree from the University of Shanghai for Science and Technology, Shanghai, China, in 2016. He is currently pursuing the Ph.D. degree with the National University of Defense Technology (NUDT), Changsha, China.
His research interests include numerical optimization, satellite scheduling, and algorithm evolution using large language models.

authors.name: Jian Wu
affiliation: Hangzhou Institute of Technology, Xidian University, Hangzhou, China

p: Jian Wu received the B.S. and M.S. degrees from Hunan University of Technology, Zhuzhou, China, in 2015 and 2018, and the Ph.D. degree from the National University of Defense Technology, Changsha, China, in 2024.

He is currently an Assistant Researcher with Hangzhou Institute of Technology, Xidian University, Xi’an, China. His research interests include intelligent optimization, mission planning, and scheduling methods.

authors.name: Guohua Wu
affiliation: School of Automation, Central South University, Changsha, China

p: Guohua Wu (Senior Member, IEEE) received the B.S. degree in information systems and the Ph.D. degree in operations research from the National University of Defense Technology, Changsha, China, in 2008 and 2014, respectively.

From 2012 to 2014, he was a Visiting Ph.D Student at the University of Alberta, Edmonton, AB, Canada. He is currently a Professor with the School of Automation, Central South University, Changsha. His research interests include scheduling, reinforcement learning, and computational intelligence. He has authored more than 180 refereed articles, including those published in IEEE Transactions on Cybernetics, IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics, and IEEE Transactions on Evolutionary Computation. His research interests include scheduling, reinforcement learning, and computational intelligence.
Dr. Wu serves as an Associate Editor for Information Sciences, Swarm and Evolutionary Computation, and Computers and Electrical Engineering.

authors.name: Lining Xing
affiliation: Research Institute of Intelligent Control and Manufacturing System, Jiangsu University of Technology, Changzhou, China

p: Lining Xing (Member, IEEE) received the joint bachelor’s degree in economics and in science from Xi’an Jiaotong University, Xi’an, China, in 2002, and the Ph.D. degree in management science from the National University of Defense Technology, Changsha, China, in 2009.

He was with the School of Computer, University of Birmingham, Birmingham, U.K., from November 2007 to 2008. He is currently a Professor with the School of Computer Engineering, Jiangsu University of Technology, Changzhou, China. His research interests include intelligent optimization methods and scheduling of resources.

authors.name: Yingwu Chen
affiliation: College of Systems Engineering, National University of Defense Technology, Changsha, China

p: Yingwu Chen received the B.Eng. degree in automation and the M.Eng. and Ph.D. degrees in systems engineering from the National University of Defense Technology, Changsha, China, in 1984, 1987, and 1994, respectively.

He has been a Distinguished Professor with the College of System Engineering, National University of Defense Technology, where he focuses on management theory and its applications. He has authored more than 70 research publications. His research interests include assistant decision-making systems for planning, decision-making systems for project evaluation, management decisions, and artificial intelligence.
Dr. Chen has been the Executive Director of the Systems Engineering Society of China since 2010.

authors.name: Yanjie Song
affiliation: College of Systems Engineering, National University of Defense Technology, Changsha, China

p: Yanjie Song (Senior Member, IEEE) received the B.S. degree in management from Tianjin University, Tianjin, China, in 2017, and the Ph.D. degree in engineering from the National University of Defense Technology, Changsha, China, in 2023.

He has published more than 60 articles in IEEE Transactions on Evolutionary Computation, IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing, and other journals. He has authored four academic books, obtained ten national invention patents, and hosted/participated in more than 15 projects. His research interests include computational intelligence, evolutionary algorithms, combinatorial optimization, and deep reinforcement learning.

Dr. Song is now a Young Editorial Board Member of Data Science and Management. He is a reviewer of IEEE Transactions on Evolutionary Computation, IEEE Transactions on Cybernetics, and more than 30 other journals. He is a Guest Editor of Swarm and Evolutionary Computation, Computers and Electrical Engineering, and International Journal on Interactive Design and Manufacturing.

abstract: The Earth Observation Satellite Task Scheduling Problem (EOSTSP) is an NP-Hard challenge critical for space-based information acquisition. Conventional optimization methods are hampered by high development costs, limited adaptability to dynamic scenarios, and poor interpretability. We propose a training-free solution that leverages the reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) through a multiagent framework. Our approach introduces an order-driven scheduling strategy that fundamentally reconceptualizes the EOSTSP as a real-time order fulfillment process, drawing inspiration from dynamic resource allocation paradigms in complex service systems. This original methodology transforms the traditionally monolithic scheduling problem into a structured sequential decision flow, where each observation task is processed as an independent order through specialized decision phases. Implemented via the Tri-Stage LLM-Coordinated (TSLC) framework, this novel approach enables autonomous scheduling through coordinated multiagent reasoning while maintaining full operational feasibility via external validation. Empirical results demonstrate performance improvements of 4.58% and 13.38% over state-of-the-art algorithms in routine and emergency scenarios, respectively, while providing transparent interpretability through its structured decision-making process, effectively overcoming the opaque limitations of traditional optimization approaches.
